title: Two ports appear twice in the frontend's port-of-entry list under different codes — Pembroke Port and Port of Sheerness — so a user picking one has to guess which of two identically named entries is the right one; DR1's list names each port once.

finding.frontend: The port-of-entry search offers seventy-eight ports, and two of them are listed twice. Pembroke Port appears under GB PED and again under GB PEM; Port of Sheerness appears under GBSHS and again under GB SHS, the second of the pair differing only by a space in the code (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:182-189, 254-261). Typing "Pembroke" returns two results with identical text, and the user has no way to tell which one the service expects — the codes are the only thing that separates them and nothing on the page explains what a code means. Whichever they pick is stored, so the same physical port arrives at the backend under two different codes depending on which line the user happened to click.
finding.prototype: DR1's catalogue names Sheerness once, under GBSHS (app/data/uk-airports.js:175), and has no Pembroke entry at all. It is not free of repeated names, though: eight places appear twice under different codes — Aberdeen, Bristol, Cardiff, Dundee, Glasgow, Inverness, Manchester and Southampton — the airport and the seaport sharing one name. DR1 prints the code after the name, so a user choosing Aberdeen picks between "Aberdeen - ABZ" and "Aberdeen - GBABD" with nothing else to separate them.
finding.difference: Nothing to build until it is settled whether one name under two codes is a defect at all, because DR1 does the same thing eight times over and both services print the code beside the name. What would settle it: the reference-data owner saying whether GB PED and GB PEM are two facilities or one record duplicated. The other pair is worth raising whatever the answer — GBSHS and "GB SHS" are the same five characters with a space gained or lost, which is a data defect on its own terms — but it belongs in a reference-data ticket rather than in this backlog, because DR1 gives no position to compare it against.
finding.falsifiedBy: DR1's own port catalogue carrying two entries that share a name and differ only by code. Already observed, on eight names, which is why this finding is disputed rather than accepted.
finding.correction: CLAIMED: the frontend lists Pembroke Port and Port of Sheerness twice while DR1 names every port once. FRONTEND LEG TRUE: the fixture holds GB PED and GB PEM both named 'Pembroke Port' and GBSHS and 'GB SHS' both named 'Port of Sheerness' (src/server/app/services/_capture/fixtures/ports-of-entry.json:182-189, 253-260), and the captured DOM renders 'Pembroke Port (GB PED)' beside 'Pembroke Port (GB PEM)'. PROTOTYPE LEG FALSE: DR1's catalogue repeats eight names under different codes — Aberdeen (ABZ and GBABD), Bristol, Cardiff, Dundee, Glasgow, Inverness, Manchester (MAN and GBMNC) and Southampton (SOU and GBSOU) — because it lists the airport and the seaport separately. The captured dr1-arrival-details DOM renders 'Aberdeen - ABZ' and 'Aberdeen - GBABD'. DR1 is the oracle and DR1 behaves the same way, so the parity claim does not stand. ALSO OVERSTATED: 'two results with identical text'. Both services append the code, so the option text is not identical — the finding's own next clause concedes the codes separate them. And DR1 has no Pembroke entry of any kind, so it takes no position on that pair. HOW CHECKED: uniq -d over the name and code literals in app/data/uk-airports.js; grep of the rendered option text in capture/html/frontend/fe-arrival-details.html and capture/html/prototype/dr1-arrival-details.html. BAND: needs-backend to disputed.

relatedTo.why: Both are defects in the same reference-data port catalogue and would be fixed in one pass
